title: The Moon
summary: Earth's only natural satellite. Its pull drives our ocean tides, and its far side always faces away from us.

title: Mars
summary: A cold, dusty desert world with the tallest volcano in the solar system and two tiny moons.

title: The Sun
summary: The star at the center of our solar system, providing light and heat to sustain life on Earth.

title: Saturn
summary: Famous for its stunning rings, Saturn is a gas giant with dozens of moons and a captivating atmosphere.

title: Jupiter
summary: The largest planet in our solar system, Jupiter is a gas giant with a powerful magnetic field and dozens of moons.

title: Andromeda Galaxy
summary: The nearest spiral galaxy to the Milky Way, Andromeda is on a collision course with our galaxy, expected to merge in about 4.5 billion years.

title: Mercury
summary: The smallest planet and the closest to the Sun, a cratered world of rock with no atmosphere to soften its swings from scorching to freezing.

title: Venus
summary: Earth's near-twin in size, wrapped in a thick carbon dioxide atmosphere that traps heat until its surface glows at 464°C.

title: Earth
summary: The only world known to harbour life, with liquid water oceans covering 71 percent of its surface and a magnetic field that shields it.

title: Uranus
summary: An ice giant tipped onto its side, rolling around the Sun with a 98-degree tilt that gives it seasons lasting 21 years each.

title: Neptune
summary: The farthest planet from the Sun, a deep-blue ice giant driven by the fastest winds measured on any planet.

title: Titan
summary: Saturn's largest moon and the only moon with a thick atmosphere, where rivers and lakes are filled with liquid methane.

title: Europa
summary: An icy Jovian moon hiding a global saltwater ocean beneath its shell — a leading candidate for life beyond Earth.

title: Io
summary: The most volcanically active world in the solar system, kept molten by the tidal grip of Jupiter and its sibling moons.

title: Ganymede
summary: The largest moon in the solar system — bigger than the planet Mercury — and the only moon with its own magnetic field.

title: Triton
summary: Neptune's largest moon orbits backwards, and its frozen surface erupts geysers of nitrogen — a captured Kuiper Belt world.

title: Sirius
summary: The brightest star in Earth's night sky, a blue-white star twice the Sun's mass with a faint white dwarf companion.

title: Rigel
summary: A blue supergiant marking the foot of Orion, shining roughly 120,000 times brighter than the Sun.

title: Betelgeuse
summary: A red supergiant on the edge of stellar death, so vast it would swallow the orbit of Jupiter if placed at our Sun.

title: Proxima Centauri
summary: The closest star to the Sun, a cool red dwarf with at least one Earth-sized planet in its habitable zone.

title: Vega
summary: The fifth-brightest star in the sky and a calibration standard for astronomers, 25 light-years away in Lyra.

title: Milky Way Galaxy
summary: Our home galaxy: a barred spiral of 100 to 400 billion stars, with a supermassive black hole at its centre.

title: Triangulum Galaxy
summary: The third-largest galaxy in our Local Group and the most distant object visible to the naked eye, 2.7 million light-years away.

title: Whirlpool Galaxy
summary: A grand-design spiral 31 million light-years away, caught mid-interaction with a smaller companion galaxy.

title: Crab Nebula
summary: The shredded remains of a supernova that Chinese astronomers recorded in 1054, now powered by a spinning neutron star.

title: Orion Nebula
summary: A stellar nursery 1,344 light-years away, and the brightest region of star formation visible to the naked eye.
